operations.description: Validate positive three-bin histograms and the finite integer-coupling grid.
Count distinct feasible integer coupling tables.
Find exact minimum and maximum normalized transport cost.
Retain every tied optimum on the declared integer grid.
Represent the independent rational coupling and its expected cost.
Compare minimum disagreement with total variation.
Compare line-metric transport with cumulative mass imbalance.
Find exact feasible bounds for each coupling cell.
Distinguish possible and forced support across all optimal grid tables.
Count grid couplings at every exact cost.
Produce a bounded integer dual-potential certificate.
Check complementary slackness on every optimal positive cell.
Test invariance of the optimal set under row and column cost shifts.
Test transposition of supply, demand and costs.
Test simultaneous relabelling of bins and cost entries.
Represent a half-and-half rational mixture of two feasible tables.
Explain finite transport results with explicit units and scope.
Measure the response to one declared cell-cost increment.
Retain missing independent and empirical evidence.
Hold real allocation and competent-authority actions.

novelty_boundary: Distinct typed transport inputs, not universal novelty or inherited execution credit.
successor_practices: compare sparse and dense transport certificates

hypothesized_laws.title: Marginal conservation
hypothesized_laws.claim: Every enumerated coupling has the declared row and column sums.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: One row or column differs from its declared marginal.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Finite feasibility
hypothesized_laws.claim: The positive equal-mass integer histograms in these fixtures have a nonempty coupling grid.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: An admitted fixture has no feasible integer table.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Gauge shift
hypothesized_laws.claim: Adding row and column costs shifts every feasible objective by the same marginal-weighted constant.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: Two feasible tables have different objective shifts.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Transpose covariance
hypothesized_laws.claim: Transposing a coupling and cost matrix while exchanging marginals preserves objective and optimality.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: The transformed optimal set or exact value differs.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Label covariance
hypothesized_laws.claim: Consistent row and column relabelling permutes the optimal tables without changing exact cost.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: An optimal table is lost or gains an unequal transformed cost.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Perturbation bound
hypothesized_laws.claim: Increasing one cell cost by one has nonnegative optimal-value change bounded by that cell mass in a prior optimum.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: The observed change is negative or exceeds the declared bound.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Independent comparison
hypothesized_laws.claim: The exact dual-certified optimum is no larger than the independent product coupling cost.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: A feasible independent coupling has cost below the certified optimum.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Weak duality
hypothesized_laws.claim: Any recorded feasible dual potentials give an objective no greater than every feasible primal table.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: A feasible dual exceeds a feasible primal objective.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Fixture dual equality
hypothesized_laws.claim: The bounded potential search yields a dual value equal to the independently enumerated primal minimum for these fixtures.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: The search yields a nonzero gap; do not infer universal failure or extend the search silently.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Complementary slackness
hypothesized_laws.claim: Positive cells of an optimal table are tight for a matching feasible dual certificate.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: An optimal positive cell has nonzero dual slack.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Mixture conservation
hypothesized_laws.claim: The declared half-and-half rational mixture preserves both marginal distributions.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: A rational row or column sum differs from the declared mass fraction.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Optimal support
hypothesized_laws.claim: The forced support is a subset of possible support across all tied grid optima.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: A forced cell is absent from the possible support.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Disagreement identity
hypothesized_laws.claim: The minimum normalized off-diagonal coupling mass equals total variation for these common labelled bins.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: Exact minimum disagreement and total variation differ.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Line identity
hypothesized_laws.claim: Absolute-index transport cost equals the sum of cumulative mass imbalances divided by total mass.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: The enumerated optimum and cumulative formula differ.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

hypothesized_laws.title: Cell bounds
hypothesized_laws.claim: Each cell ranges from max(0,a_i+b_j-M) through min(a_i,b_j) on these finite coupling grids.
hypothesized_laws.falsifier: An enumerated extremum differs from either exact cell bound.
hypothesized_laws.scope: All fifteen declared profiles; no original universal-law or empirical claim

open_problem_probes.question: What independently observed data could justify the marginal counts?
Which defensible units and measurement procedure could justify the cost matrix?
How should uncertainty in marginals be represented without treating invented fixtures as data?
When is the integer mass grid an appropriate model rather than an arbitrary discretization?
How would externally justified capacity or prohibited-route constraints change feasibility?
How should unequal total masses be modeled with explicit creation or disposal assumptions?
Which independently justified interval-cost model would support robust optimization?
How would negative or unbounded costs change the finite admission and certificate bounds?
What evidence would support scalability beyond the declared three-bin six-unit limits?
Can an independent implementation reproduce the exact tables and identify discrepancies?
Which bin-coarsening choices preserve meaning in a real application?
What assistive-technology and participant testing would establish usable access to the viewer?
What consent and data-purpose limits would apply before any participant records were used?
Who has authority to accept an allocation and provide appeal or remedy for affected parties?
Which culturally competent and Maori-authority processes would govern any relevant application?
